messages.author: fb7f17a1e7de9977
messages.subject: \Sexpr with scientific notation inside $...$
parts:
I'm not sure if this is a knitr bug or if I'm doing something wrong. If I knit the following minimal example:

\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
<<>>=
  x <- 10^10
@
$x = \Sexpr{x}$.
\end{document}

$x = \Sexpr{x}$ gets turned into $x = $10^{10}$$ in the .tex file, which causes a pdlatex error. Is this a user error or something I can avoid? I could move \Sexpr{x} outside of $ here, but for a more complex formula, I don't think it will work.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] \Sexpr with scientific notation inside $...$
parts:
Sorry I did not consider this case. I have added a fix to the
development version: https://github.com/yihui/knitr Basically you can
write the numbers in I() so knitr will not add $$ automatically, e.g.
$x = \Sexpr{I(x)}$.

Regards,
Yihui
